clue.text: Experimental examination scheme for a high-flier

parts.note: an experimental examination is a test, a trial run to see how something performs
a pilot is a trial scheme, as in a pilot project run before a full launch

explanation.surface: Someone describes a trial assessment programme designed for an ambitious high achiever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flier' suggests a star executive, but it is literal: someone who flies new aircraft to try them out.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who flies new aircraft to try them out is literally a high flier.

clue.text: Each service rendered to make money

parts.note: EA is the standard abbreviation for each, as on price labels
RN, the Royal Navy, is one of the armed services

explanation.surface: Each favour done for someone is a way of bringing in cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service' looks like a favour done, but in crosswords one of the armed services is often meant: here RN, the Royal Navy.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to receive income in return for work.

clue.text: Time to get E European currency out of difficulty

parts.note: the rouble is the currency of Russia, in eastern Europe

explanation.surface: A suggestion that a moment for a strong eastern currency will rescue someone from hardship.
explanation.definitionFit: Trouble and difficulty are synonyms for a problem or hardship.

clue.text: Sluggishness shown in hesitation by Spanish aunt

parts.note: taken as written
er is the sound people make when they hesitate
tia is Spanish for aunt

explanation.surface: An aunt in Spain displays lethargy by being hesitant.
explanation.definitionFit: Inertia is a tendency to stay still, a lack of energy or drive.

clue.text: Outstanding wife immersed in a dictionary

indicators.note: something immersed in another thing is placed inside it, so one letter sits within the dictionary's letters

parts.note: the OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
W is the usual abbreviation for wife, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: An excellent wife is completely absorbed in reading a dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' seems to praise the wife, but it means still unpaid.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt that is outstanding is still unpaid and owing.

clue.text: Bowling session by the Australian captain in Scotland

parts.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls delivered by one bowler
taken as written
Allan Border captained the Australian cricket team from 1984 to 1994

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: a spell of bowling bowled by Australia's skipper during a match in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: From England, Scotland lies over the border, so the location reads as the definition. Cricket's over is a set of six deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: To someone in England, Scotland is the country across the frontier to the north.

clue.text: Practise how to be a pickpocket

definitions.meaning: to regain skill by doing something again, to warm up for it
a pickpocket literally has to slip a hand inside a pocket

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to practise to regain skill, while a thief literally slides a hand into another person's pocket.

clue.text: Look away as every one asset is removed

indicators.note: removed means the letters are taken from their places and shifted into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Everyone turns away in embarrassment as each holding is stripped from the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Removed' reads as assets being stripped, but it is the anagram signal for EVERY ONE ASSET.
explanation.definitionFit: To avert your gaze is to turn your sight away from something.

clue.text: Mother has a picture inlaid in metal

parts.note: a dam is the mother of an animal, such as a horse
a scene is a view or a picture of a place

explanation.surface: Mum owns a painting set into metalwork.
explanation.walkthrough: Damascene work, named after Damascus, is metal inlaid with gold or silver patterns.
explanation.definitionFit: Damascene describes metalwork decorated with inlaid gold or silver, a craft linked with Damascus.

clue.text: Cease trading near N Ireland county

parts.note: close means near, as in close by
Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A shop near a county in Northern Ireland stops doing business.
explanation.definitionFit: A business that shuts permanently stops operating altogether.

clue.text: Piece of land Saladin failed to save

definitions.meaning: a unit of land area, 4,840 square yards
the port city captured from Saladin by the Crusaders in 1191 during the Third Crusade

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a unit of land measure and the city in Israel that the sultan Saladin lost to Richard the Lionheart in 1191.

clue.text: Calm seaman took a meal

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a rank of sailor
ate means took a meal

explanation.surface: A peaceful sailor sat down to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: To abate is to lessen in force, as a storm calms down.

clue.text: One silly enough to produce pured fruit

definitions.meaning: a silly person, a dimwit or idiot
a cold dessert of puréed fruit folded into cream or custard

explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'pured' is puréed without its accent and one letter. The dessert is a British pudding of crushed fruit blended with cream or custard.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an idiot and a British dessert of crushed fruit mixed with cream, such as gooseberry.

clue.text: The man will love to get a greeting

parts.note: the man will contracts to he'll, the letters HELL without apostrophe
love means zero in tennis scoring, shown as the letter O

explanation.surface: A man will offer love in order to receive a friendly salute.
explanation.definitionFit: Hello is the commonest salutation when people meet.

clue.text: Strike a small, small coin

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a mite was a small coin, as in the widow's mite of the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone hits a tiny little coin.
explanation.definitionFit: To smite is an old word meaning to hit hard.

clue.text: Succeed in getting a Greek cross the day before

parts.note: chi is the Greek letter shaped like a cross, X
an eve is the day before an event, as Christmas Eve

explanation.surface: Someone manages to obtain a cross from Greece the previous day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek cross' sounds like an ecclesiastical symbol, but it is the letter chi, written X.
explanation.definitionFit: To achieve is to succeed in reaching a goal.

clue.text: Wandering for miles, as wildly as can be

indicators.note: wildly signals that the letters are tossed about into a new order

explanation.surface: A hiker roams for miles as freely as possible.
explanation.definitionFit: Aimless means without purpose or direction, drifting about.

clue.text: Last man taken in as apprentice by Australian friend

indicators.note: a person taken in is housed inside, so one letter goes within the friend's letters

parts.note: cobber is Australian slang for a mate
L stands for learner, as on L-plates for learner drivers

explanation.surface: A final man is accepted as a trainee by a mate from Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' is a shoemaker's foot-shaped form, not 'final', so the last man is a shoemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoemaker works on a last, the wooden foot model, so is the last man.

clue.text: Withdraw into monastic seclusion

definitions.meaning: to pull back or fall back
a period of prayer and quiet away from the world

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to pull back, as an army does, and a period of religious withdrawal from everyday life.

clue.text: Henry yearned to get wed

parts.note: H is the symbol of the henry, the unit of inductance
itched means longed or yearned, as in itching to go

explanation.surface: Henry longed to marry.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting hitched is informal for getting married.

clue.text: Hollow-cheeked harridan has to pull back

parts.note: a harridan is a bossy old woman, a hag

indicators.note: to pull back signals that the word for pull is read in reverse

parts.note: drag means pull

explanation.surface: A gaunt old crone must retreat.
explanation.definitionFit: Haggard means gaunt and worn-looking from exhaustion or worry.

clue.text: Average number joining the Marines

parts.note: number gives NO
RM stands for the Royal Marines

explanation.surface: An ordinary number of recruits sign up with the Marines.
explanation.definitionFit: The norm is the usual standard, what is typical or average.

clue.text: The way to get on to the platform

definitions.meaning: a step in a process by which one progresses or gets ahead
a raised floor on which performers appear

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a step of progress and the raised floor of a theatre.

clue.text: Wintry weather in the South at present

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for south
now means at present

explanation.surface: A report of cold conditions currently in southern regions.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow is frozen precipitation typical of winter.

clue.text: One faint reflection from the R south of France

indicators.note: a reflection in a mirror shows things the wrong way round, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
dim means faint

explanation.surface: A single faint mirror image comes from southern France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflection' reverses I and DIM. The Midi is the name for the south of France.
explanation.definitionFit: The Midi is the common French name for the southern part of the country.

clue.text: Group of five accommodated by Ottoman officer

indicators.note: something accommodated by another is housed within it, so one letter goes inside the officer's letters

parts.note: a bey was a governor or official in the Ottoman Empire
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: A party of five people put up by a Turkish official.
explanation.definitionFit: A bevy is a company, a collection of people or birds.

clue.text: Think about Samuel's mentor perpetrating perjury

indicators.note: about means going round, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: to deliberate is to think carefully
Eli was the priest who raised the prophet Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: Considering a biblical priest who committed perjury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perpetrating' reads as part of the definition but is only a link. 'About' signals the container; Eli is the priest in the First Book of Samuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Perjury is knowingly telling untruths under oath, a calculated falsehood.

clue.text: Bath is dry, strangely enough, for annual celebrations

indicators.note: strangely signals that the letters are put into an unusual new order

explanation.surface: Odd as it seems, a dry bath is part of yearly festivities.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's birthday is celebrated once each year.
